LandingMetadata.title: Palworld Server Console | Save Sync & Guild Breeding - PalBeacon
LandingMetadata.description: PalBeacon is a Palworld server console for read-only save sync, shared guild inventory, and collaborative multi-generation breeding plans.
LandingMetadata.keywords: Palworld save sync,Palworld inventory,Palworld breeding planner,Palworld breeding calculator,Palworld passive skills,Palworld guild inventory
LandingMetadata.ogLineTwo: Build a breeding plan you can follow

PublicContent.homeCardTitle: Back to the PalBeacon home page
PublicContent.exploreDescription: Start with the question you need to solve, from safe save sync to guild-based breeding routes.
PublicContent.saveSyncMetadataDescription: Connect a Palworld server save to the PalBeacon console with a read-only client that uploads sanitized player, guild, and Pal inventory data.
PublicContent.saveSyncCardDescription: Install the read-only client, connect one world, and sync only the sanitized inventory data the console needs.
PublicContent.saveSyncIntro: Use palbeacon-cli to connect a self-hosted Palworld world save to PalBeacon. The client checks source files read-only on the server host, parses a safe copy, and sends only the sanitized inventory data required by the console.
PublicContent.saveSyncCta: Sign in and create a sync device
PublicContent.saveSyncCtaBody: Sign in to create a sync device and copy its one-time pairing code, then initialize the client on the host that stores your world save.
PublicContent.saveSyncPurposeTitle: Why the console needs save sync
PublicContent.saveSyncPurposeBody: PalBeacon does not pull inventory through a game-server control interface. A sync device brings current player, guild, and Pal facts into the console so inventory, data status, and breeding routes use one snapshot.
PublicContent.saveSyncPurposePointOne: Create a sync device in your account, then copy its one-time pairing code.
PublicContent.saveSyncPurposePointTwo: Device status shows the latest sync time, latest result, and whether authorization remains valid.
PublicContent.saveSyncPurposePointThree: After the first sync, players can claim their in-game character by nickname.
PublicContent.saveSyncInstallBody: The current npm package supports Linux x64 and Windows x64 and requires Node.js 22 or later. Both platforms use the same install command, and the package selects its bundled parser automatically.
PublicContent.saveSyncInstallPointOne: palbeacon init validates the platform and path, pairs the device, and saves per-user configuration; it does not perform the first sync.
PublicContent.saveSyncInstallPointTwo: The client does not download or compile a parser at runtime and needs no Python, compiler, or extra runtime.
PublicContent.saveSyncWorldBody: Enter the target world directory containing Level.sav and Players/, or a parent that contains only one world. The client searches to a controlled depth for one Level.sav and rejects symlinks and paths that are too broad.
PublicContent.saveSyncWorldPointOne: Paths may contain spaces or Unicode, and Windows drive-letter paths are supported.
PublicContent.saveSyncWorldPointTwo: If several worlds are found, the client asks you to narrow the path instead of guessing.
PublicContent.saveSyncWorldPointThree: Browser uploads, macOS, other architectures, and local single-player saves are not currently supported.
PublicContent.saveSyncRunBody: palbeacon run is a foreground process. It syncs immediately on startup, then checks for save changes every 300 seconds by default; keep it running for continued updates.
PublicContent.saveSyncRunPointOne: When the save is unchanged, the client sends a device heartbeat without parsing or uploading inventory again.
PublicContent.saveSyncRunPointTwo: A temporary network or parser failure affects only that cycle; revoked device access stops the process and asks you to pair again.
PublicContent.saveSyncRunPointThree: After publication, check sync status in the console and select your nickname from the unclaimed characters.
PublicContent.saveSyncSafetyTitle: Source save, temporary copy, and upload boundary
PublicContent.saveSyncSafetyBody: Every cycle checks that source files are stable, copies Level.sav and character saves from Players/ into a per-user temporary directory, and gives only that copy to the parser. Temporary files are removed afterward.
PublicContent.saveSyncSafetyPointOne: The client never modifies the real save and never runs save, restart, or other server control commands.
PublicContent.saveSyncSafetyPointTwo: The complete save is never uploaded to PalBeacon; parsing happens on the safe copy on your server host.
PublicContent.saveSyncSafetyPointThree: Uploads are limited to player, guild, Pal, passive, gender, owner, and location facts required by inventory and breeding.
PublicContent.saveSyncSafetyPointFour: World, player, guild, Pal instance, and location identifiers are hashed before upload, and raw parser metadata is removed.
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqOneQuestion: Which machine should run the sync client?
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqOneAnswer: Run it on a Linux x64 or Windows x64 host that can read the target server world save, with Node.js 22 or later installed.
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqTwoQuestion: Does palbeacon init upload the save immediately?
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqTwoAnswer: No. init validates the platform and directory, pairs the device, and saves configuration. The first sync starts immediately when you run palbeacon run.
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqThreeQuestion: What if one directory contains several worlds?
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqThreeAnswer: Point the client at the world containing the target Level.sav and Players/. It stops when several worlds are found and never chooses one for you.
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqFourQuestion: Does PalBeacon upload the complete Level.sav?
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqFourAnswer: No. Level.sav and character saves are copied only to a local temporary directory for parsing. The cloud receives sanitized data needed by inventory and breeding features.
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqFiveQuestion: Will a failed sync repair or modify the game save?
PublicContent.saveSyncFaqFiveAnswer: No. A failure affects only that sync cycle. The client never writes back, repairs the save, or controls the game server.
PublicContent.savePlannerMetadataDescription: Build practical Palworld breeding routes from real save inventory, shared guild Pals, passive distribution, and usable intermediate parents.
PublicContent.savePlannerCardDescription: Start from real player and guild inventory, then compare multi-generation routes with parents you can actually find.
PublicContent.savePlannerIntro: A typical breeding calculator tells you which Pal species can produce a target. PalBeacon also reads a current inventory snapshot, finds where desired passives are spread across instances, and turns legal species relationships into multi-generation routes you can inspect, compare, and save.
PublicContent.savePlannerCtaTitle: Start with the Pals you actually have
PublicContent.savePlannerCtaBody: Open the breeder, choose a target Pal and up to four desired passives, and let the existing authentication flow handle sign-in when needed.
PublicContent.savePlannerDifferenceBody: Species recipes are only the first layer. A usable route also needs to know whether parents exist, how passives are distributed, gender, owner, location, and sharing permission.
PublicContent.savePlannerDifferencePointOne: A typical calculator lists parent combinations that can produce the target species.
PublicContent.savePlannerDifferencePointTwo: PalBeacon validates every step against fixed game data and never lets AI invent recipes.
PublicContent.savePlannerDifferencePointThree: Routes with the same species and passive topology are deduplicated so comparisons stay meaningful.
PublicContent.savePlannerInventoryTitle: Read real inventory and passive distribution
PublicContent.savePlannerInventoryBody: Each calculation starts from a fixed synchronized inventory snapshot. It uses all of the player's available Pals plus same-guild candidates that are permitted for sharing, rather than assuming arbitrary parents already exist.
PublicContent.savePlannerInventoryPointOne: Desired passives may be distributed across several individual Pals.
PublicContent.savePlannerInventoryPointTwo: Candidates keep their real gender, instance, owner, and provable location.
PublicContent.savePlannerInventoryPointThree: Another player's complete private inventory never enters your candidate pool without sharing permission.
PublicContent.savePlannerIntermediateBody: A route can first combine existing Pals, carry the required passives into intermediate offspring, and use those intermediates in later steps. It does not require a starting parent that already has every desired passive and may be harder to obtain than the final target.
PublicContent.savePlannerIntermediatePointOne: The algorithm plans intermediate parents and the desired passives that must be retained at each generation.
PublicContent.savePlannerIntermediatePointTwo: When inventory is incomplete, a legal route can still state the missing species, gender, and passives precisely.
PublicContent.savePlannerIntermediatePointThree: Maximum generations, inventory coverage, and borrowing all contribute to feasibility and ranking.
PublicContent.savePlannerRoutesTitle: Assign instances, compare routes, and save one
PublicContent.savePlannerRoutesBody: After validating species steps, PalBeacon assigns real inventory instances, compares candidates for the selected preference, and saves chosen routes under My Plans for read-only reference.
PublicContent.savePlannerRoutesPointOne: Compare balanced, fastest, highest-success, and least-borrowing ranking views.
PublicContent.savePlannerRoutesPointTwo: The route tree shows parents, intermediates, gender, passives, owner, and location.
PublicContent.savePlannerRoutesPointThree: Both inventory-ready and legally incomplete routes can be saved, but saving never locks an instance.
PublicContent.savePlannerLimitsBody: Fixed recipes make the route legal, but passive inheritance remains random. PalBeacon does not invent precise probabilities, automate the game, or advance breeding steps for players.
PublicContent.savePlannerLimitsPointOne: Without verified probability data, difficulty and attempt ranges are strategy estimates rather than promises.
PublicContent.savePlannerLimitsPointTwo: My Plans is currently a read-only route collection with no approvals, progress tracking, or offspring confirmation.
PublicContent.savePlannerLimitsPointThree: A new save sync updates current inventory so you can recalculate, but it does not automatically detect or confirm new offspring.
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqOneQuestion: How is this different from a normal breeding calculator?
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqOneAnswer: A normal calculator mainly explains species relationships. PalBeacon combines fixed recipes with real inventory, passives, gender, owner, location, and sharing permission.
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqTwoQuestion: Do I need a parent with all four desired passives?
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqTwoAnswer: No. A route can use several existing Pals to create intermediate parents and concentrate desired passives over multiple generations.
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqThreeQuestion: Does a route guarantee passive inheritance on the first attempt?
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqThreeAnswer: No. Route legality is deterministic, but inheritance remains random. The page never promises an unverified exact success rate.
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqFourQuestion: Will a new sync advance my saved plan automatically?
PublicContent.savePlannerFaqFourAnswer: No. A new sync updates current inventory so you can recalculate. Saved routes stay read-only and do not detect offspring or change progress automatically.
PublicContent.passiveRouteMetadataDescription: Learn how to combine passives across existing and shared guild Pals, build intermediate parents, and follow a practical multi-generation route.
PublicContent.passiveRouteCardDescription: Understand how intermediate parents, unwanted passives, gender, and a multi-generation tree affect execution.
PublicContent.passiveRouteIntro: When desired passives are spread across different Pals, waiting for one perfect parent is often impractical. PalBeacon uses fixed breeding relationships and currently accessible inventory to build a route tree in which intermediate parents bring those passives together over generations.
PublicContent.passiveRouteCtaTitle: Turn scattered passives into a clear route
PublicContent.passiveRouteCtaBody: Choose a target Pal and up to four passives in the breeder, then see which routes current inventory supports and what is still missing.
PublicContent.passiveRouteDistributionBody: Server inventory comes from different players, captures, and breeding results. The passives for one target are often spread across different species and instances, while gender and species combinations limit which Pals can pair directly.
PublicContent.passiveRouteDistributionPointOne: Finding a suitable parent that already has four desired passives is often harder than planning intermediates.
PublicContent.passiveRouteDistributionPointTwo: PalBeacon measures which desired passives each instance covers instead of looking only at species.
PublicContent.passiveRouteDistributionPointThree: Personal inventory and permitted guild Pals can cover the desired set together.
PublicContent.passiveRouteIntermediateBody: First-generation offspring may carry only part of the desired set, then pair with another inventory parent or intermediate in a later step. Each checkpoint states what the next generation needs to retain.
PublicContent.passiveRouteIntermediatePointOne: Intermediate parents connect several starting instances into an executable dependency chain.
PublicContent.passiveRouteIntermediatePointTwo: Species transitions, viable gender, or passive concentration can all add generations.
PublicContent.passiveRouteIntermediatePointThree: A missing starting parent appears as a requirement, never as a fabricated inventory instance.
PublicContent.passiveRouteConstraintsTitle: Unwanted passives, gender, and species recipes
PublicContent.passiveRouteConstraintsBody: Unwanted parent passives add inheritance noise, so PalBeacon prefers an inventory representative with fewer extras for the same route. Gender must work for each step, and offspring species always comes from the fixed breeding data version.
PublicContent.passiveRouteConstraintsPointOne: Unwanted passives do not change recipe legality, but they can make inheritance harder.
PublicContent.passiveRouteConstraintsPointTwo: Same-species steps need viable opposite-sex instances, and different-species steps still require compatible genders.
PublicContent.passiveRouteConstraintsPointThree: AI may explain or assist ranking, but cannot change species relationships or base scores.
PublicContent.passiveRouteReadingTitle: How to read a route tree
PublicContent.passiveRouteReadingBody: Start with inventory parents on the left, follow their connectors into intermediate offspring, and continue toward the final target. Nodes distinguish real inventory, intermediate products, the target, and missing requirements.
PublicContent.passiveRouteReadingPointOne: Parent nodes show actual passives, gender, owner, and a provable location.
PublicContent.passiveRouteReadingPointTwo: Intermediate and target nodes show the passives the route needs to retain.
PublicContent.passiveRouteReadingPointThree: Generations, borrowed Pals, inventory coverage, and missing summaries help compare execution cost.
PublicContent.passiveRouteRandomnessTitle: A legal route does not make outcomes certain
PublicContent.passiveRouteRandomnessBody: The tree fixes legal breeding steps and desired checkpoints, but passive results from each hatch remain random. A step may need repeats, and the complete route may need several generations.
PublicContent.passiveRouteRandomnessPointOne: PalBeacon never promises a first try, guaranteed four gold passives, or an unverified exact probability.
PublicContent.passiveRouteRandomnessPointTwo: After syncing new inventory, recalculate to use newly available parents in a revised route.
PublicContent.passiveRouteRandomnessPointThree: Saved routes do not detect offspring automatically, advance progress, or operate the game.
PublicContent.passiveRouteDiagramTitle: How one route brings requirements together
PublicContent.passiveRouteDiagramCaption: This diagram shows dependencies only. Actual species, gender, and recipes come from fixed game data and current inventory.
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqOneQuestion: Why does a route need intermediate parents?
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqOneAnswer: Desired passives and the target species may not fit into one step. Intermediates combine part of the passive set before entering later legal recipes.
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqTwoQuestion: Do unwanted passives make a recipe invalid?
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqTwoAnswer: They do not change a fixed species recipe, but they add inheritance noise. PalBeacon prefers instances with fewer extras within the same route.
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqThreeAnswer: Each breeding step needs two gender-compatible instances. A species relationship without the required real genders cannot be executed directly from current inventory.
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqFourQuestion: Does a multi-generation route guarantee the final passives?
PublicContent.passiveRouteFaqFourAnswer: No. The route guarantees that steps use fixed legal relationships, but passive inheritance remains random and may require repeated attempts.
PublicContent.guildInventoryMetadataDescription: Sync guild Pal inventories into one server console, control sharing, find usable parents, and collaborate on breeding routes and saved plans.
PublicContent.guildInventoryCardDescription: Find parents within player-controlled sharing boundaries and coordinate manually with owner and location details.
PublicContent.guildInventoryIntro: Private servers often have several players with different Pals and passives. One PalBeacon save sync identifies players, characters, guilds, and inventory so members can find usable parents, calculate routes, and coordinate breeding within controlled sharing boundaries.
PublicContent.guildInventoryCtaTitle: Bring permitted guild inventory into one console
PublicContent.guildInventoryCtaBody: Create a sync device and connect the server world save. After the first sync, each player can claim an in-game character and manage what they share.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPlayersTitle: Identify server players and game characters
PublicContent.guildInventoryPlayersBody: A synchronized snapshot contains world, player, guild, and Pal facts. A signed-in user selects their nickname from unclaimed characters to connect the web account to the game character.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPlayersPointOne: One private server may contain several players and guild members.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPlayersPointTwo: After claiming a character, a player can see their complete Pal inventory.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPlayersPointThree: Sync status shows when inventory was updated so members can avoid stale information.
PublicContent.guildInventorySharingTitle: Personal inventory and permitted guild inventory
PublicContent.guildInventorySharingBody: Personal inventory supports the owner's searches and breeding. Same-guild Pals explicitly permitted for sharing, plus provable guild-owned base workers, can enter the guild candidate pool.
PublicContent.guildInventorySharingPointOne: Newly found player-owned Pals are shareable by default, and the owner can turn sharing off.
PublicContent.guildInventorySharingPointTwo: Sharing preferences follow stable instances and reset safely if ownership changes.
PublicContent.guildInventorySharingPointThree: Guild scope is not a public web page; candidate data appears only after sign-in and permission checks.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPrivacyTitle: Share necessary facts, not complete private inventories
PublicContent.guildInventoryPrivacyBody: Joining the same guild does not reveal another player's complete private inventory. Breeding calculations and routes use only candidates the requester may access and expose only what is needed to borrow a Pal.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPrivacyPointOne: Another player's Pal with sharing disabled never enters your breeding candidates.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPrivacyPointTwo: A borrowed node can show species, gender, passives, owner, and a provable location.
PublicContent.guildInventoryPrivacyPointThree: Instances with unresolved ownership or dimensional-storage access are conservatively excluded.
PublicContent.guildInventoryBreedingTitle: Calculate routes with permitted guild Pals
PublicContent.guildInventoryBreedingBody: The breeder combines personal inventory with permitted guild candidates, assigns real instances, and counts borrowing. Members can compare a shorter route with one that needs fewer borrowed Pals and choose the practical tradeoff.
PublicContent.guildInventoryBreedingPointOne: Routes always validate recipes against fixed game data; sharing never changes legality.
PublicContent.guildInventoryBreedingPointTwo: Owner and location details help members identify the exact Pal to borrow in game.
PublicContent.guildInventoryBreedingPointThree: When inventory is incomplete, the route states the missing species, gender, and passives.
PublicContent.guildInventoryCollaborationTitle: Work together, with players coordinating manually
PublicContent.guildInventoryCollaborationBody: Guild members can refer to the same saved route, its parents, intermediates, and gaps, then recalculate from the latest synchronized inventory. Borrowing, hatching, and handoff still happen manually in game.
PublicContent.guildInventoryCollaborationPointOne: There is currently no chat, approval, or automatic borrowing workflow.
PublicContent.guildInventoryCollaborationPointTwo: Saving a route does not lock instances or track manual step progress.
PublicContent.guildInventoryCollaborationPointThree: A new sync updates inventory and data status but does not confirm offspring or advance a plan.
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqOneQuestion: Can other guild members see all of my Pals?
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqOneAnswer: No. Your complete personal inventory remains visible only to you. Other members see only necessary facts for shared Pals in permitted candidates and routes.
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqTwoQuestion: Who can change a Pal's sharing setting?
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqTwoAnswer: A regular player can manage sharing only for Pals they currently own. Other players cannot turn your sharing on or off.
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqThreeQuestion: Which guild Pals can the breeder use?
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqThreeAnswer: Only same-guild candidates that are permitted for access, including shared member Pals and guild inventory with provable ownership and access scope.
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqFourQuestion: Does PalBeacon approve or borrow a Pal automatically?
PublicContent.guildInventoryFaqFourAnswer: No. It provides owner, location, and route facts. Members still communicate, borrow, and execute the route manually in game.

Landing.heroDescription: Sync server saves with a read-only client, manage player and guild Pal inventories in one console, and collaborate on practical multi-generation breeding plans.
Landing.workflowTitle: Connect your server in four steps
Landing.workflowDescription: Set it up once, then PalBeacon keeps the console current while the sync client is running.
Landing.workflowStepOneTitle: Sign in and create a device
Landing.workflowStepOneBody: Create a sync device after signing in, then copy its pairing code.
Landing.workflowStepTwoBody: Install it on the Linux x64 or Windows x64 host running your Palworld server. Node.js 22 or later is required.
Landing.workflowStepThreeBody: Use palbeacon init with the world directory containing Level.sav and Players/. If you have several worlds, point it directly at the one you want. palbeacon run syncs immediately, then checks for changes every five minutes by default.
Landing.workflowStepFourBody: After the first sync, find your in-game nickname and select “This is me” to open inventory, breeding, and saved plans.
Landing.carouselInventoryHint: Your inventory and permitted guild Pals stay together in one view.
Landing.featuresTitle: See your server at a glance
Landing.featuresDescription: Turn every sync into a clear next step, from inventory to breeding routes.
Landing.systemFlowTitle: From your server to your browser
Landing.systemFlowDescription: The sync client connects outward from your server, so PalBeacon needs no new inbound port.
Landing.systemFlowClientBody: Checks changes and parses a safe copy
Landing.systemFlowCloudBody: Keeps the data your console needs
Landing.inventoryBody: View your Pals and permitted guild inventory in one console. Filter by species, gender, passives, owner, and location, and see whether the data is current.
Landing.breedingBody: Choose a target Pal and up to four passives, compare legal routes, and make the most of parents you already have.
Landing.plansBody: Save routes that are ready or still missing Pals, then revisit parents, intermediate offspring, generations, and estimated attempts.
Landing.safetyTitle: Your save stays on your server
Landing.safetyDescription: The sync client submits only what the console needs, and you can revoke a device at any time.
Landing.safetyReadOnlyTitle: The source save is never modified
Landing.safetyReadOnlyBody: The client checks the source files read-only, creates a safe local copy once they are stable, and parses that copy. It never runs server control commands.
Landing.safetyUploadTitle: The complete save is not uploaded
Landing.safetyUploadBody: Level.sav and character saves stay on your server. Only the sanitized data needed by the console is uploaded.
Landing.safetyCredentialTitle: Revoke a device at any time
Landing.safetyCredentialBody: Device credentials stay in the current user's private configuration directory. Revoking the device from the web ends its sync access.
Landing.safetyBoundaryTitle: Good data remains available after a failure
Landing.safetyBoundaryBody: Your browser cannot access administrative server keys. Inventory updates only after a complete parse, so the last valid data remains available if parsing fails.
Landing.faqTitle: A few things to know before you start
Landing.faqOneQuestion: Which saves does PalBeacon currently support?
Landing.faqOneAnswer: PalBeacon currently targets self-hosted Palworld servers. The CLI supports Linux x64 and Windows x64 and requires Node.js 22+. macOS, other architectures, browser uploads, and local single-player saves are not currently supported.
Landing.faqTwoQuestion: Will the sync client modify my save?
Landing.faqTwoAnswer: No. It checks the source files read-only, parses a safe local copy, and never runs server control commands.
Landing.faqThreeQuestion: Does it upload the complete save?
Landing.faqThreeAnswer: No. The complete save stays on your server; only sanitized data needed by the console is uploaded.
Landing.faqFourQuestion: Which save directory should I select?
Landing.faqFourAnswer: Choose the world directory containing Level.sav and Players/. palbeacon init validates it before connecting.
Landing.faqFiveQuestion: What if I have multiple worlds?
Landing.faqFiveAnswer: Point the path directly at the world you want. If it contains several worlds, the CLI asks you to narrow the path instead of guessing.
Landing.faqSixAnswer: palbeacon run syncs immediately, then checks every five minutes by default. Keep it running for continuous updates.
Landing.faqSevenQuestion: How do I match my in-game character?
Landing.faqSevenAnswer: After the first sync, find your in-game nickname among unclaimed characters and select “This is me.”
Landing.faqEightQuestion: Does a breeding route guarantee success on the first try?
Landing.faqEightAnswer: No. Routes use fixed game data, but passive inheritance is still random. Estimated attempts are guidance, not a first-try guarantee.
Landing.faqNineQuestion: Why can a route take several generations?
Landing.faqNineAnswer: Desired passives may be spread across several Pals, and the target species may need specific breeding relationships. Intermediate parents bring those requirements together over time.
Landing.footerDisclaimer: PalBeacon is an independent community tool and is not affiliated with Pocketpair.
Landing.softwareDescription: A browser console for private Palworld servers that brings inventory, data status, multi-generation breeding routes, and saved plans into one place.
Landing.softwareRequirements: The web app works in a modern browser; the save sync CLI currently requires Linux x64 or Windows x64 and Node.js 22+.

Admin.shellDescription: Review real operational summaries and perform audited actions. Every server request verifies authorization; navigation visibility is not authorization.
Admin.deniedDescription: The user is signed in, but the server-side role check did not pass.
Admin.overviewDescription: Only sanitized operational summaries are shown. Secrets, tokens, public IPs, paths, raw save names, stack traces and SQL are excluded.
Admin.staleDescription: The latest heartbeat is stale, so the current state may not be live.
Admin.bindingsDescription: Supabase users and game players remain one-to-one. Every change uses idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency and immutable audit records.
Admin.searchBindingPlaceholder: Search safe display names or player nicknames
Admin.gameDataDescription: Historical versions are immutable. Publishing and rollback only use validated catalogs and explicit confirmation. The browser never holds the Service Role.
Admin.uploadRules: PAK, UTOC, UCAS, USMAP, saves, DLLs, executables, images and audio are forbidden. The Agent revalidates the allowlist, size, SHA-256, manifest and seven relation categories.
Admin.jobsDescription: Jobs may only be retried, cancelled or have confirmed stale locks reaped. Pinned snapshots, catalog versions, routes and scores cannot be edited.
Admin.saveParserDescription: Administrator actions enter a private database command queue. The Agent polls it and executes a fixed allowlist only.
Admin.saveWorkerStale: STALE: Save Worker heartbeat is stale.
Admin.name: Name
Admin.noUnsafeControls: No shell, path, Steam update, Docker or Palworld/mihomo restart controls are provided.
Admin.settingsDescription: Only non-secret settings are managed here. Secrets expose configured/not_configured and latest check time, never their values.
Admin.rollbackDescription: Rollback appends a new version and never modifies or deletes history.
Admin.errorDescription: Security boundaries remain intact; this page did not fall back to cross-user caches or privileged keys.
Admin.confirmDescription: This operation writes an administrator audit record. Enter the full confirmation text below to continue:
Admin.uploadInitial: Only normalized .tar.zst files up to 64 MiB are accepted.
Admin.uploadInvalid: CATALOG_UPLOAD_INVALID: file type or size is not allowed.
Admin.uploadHashing: Calculating SHA-256 and requesting a private upload path…
Admin.uploadingPrivate: Uploading to the restricted private object path…
Admin.uploadComplete: Upload complete. Run validate; the Agent will verify size, SHA-256, member allowlist and catalog contract again.

Sync.claimTitle: Save synchronized: which character is yours?
Sync.claimDescription: Only unclaimed characters in the latest snapshot of your synchronized world are listed.
Sync.claimFailed: Character claim failed. Another account may have claimed it.
Sync.faqDescription: Use these notes to confirm character matching, save selection, and data safety before your first sync.
Sync.faqMatchingAnswer: After the first sync, unclaimed characters from that world appear here. Find your in-game nickname and select “This is me” to finish matching.
Sync.faqSaveDirectoryQuestion: Which Palworld save directory should I choose?
Sync.faqSaveDirectoryAnswer: Choose the world directory containing Level.sav and the Players folder. init validates the structure; if you have several worlds, select the one you want to sync.
Sync.faqSafetyAnswer: The tool reads the save and creates a safe local copy. It uploads only sanitized inventory data needed for breeding, never changes the live save, and never uploads the complete save.

DataStatus.healthyDescription: Server data is synchronized and the world state is visible.
DataStatus.staleDescription: Inventory has not synced for over 15 minutes. Verify current holdings carefully.
DataStatus.parseErrorDescription: The latest parse failed, so the last valid inventory remains in use.
DataStatus.emptyDescription: No published, sanitized inventory is available for this character yet.
DataStatus.publishedDescription: This world is using a published, pinned game-data version.
DataStatus.notConfiguredDescription: This world has no active game-data version.
DataStatus.reviewPendingDescription: A breeding-data version awaits review while the published version remains active.
DataStatus.blockedDescription: Candidate validation failed or the algorithm configuration is incomplete.
DataStatus.title: Server Data Status
DataStatus.description: Review synchronization, parsing and version status between PalBeacon and the game save.
DataStatus.previousSnapshotDetail: The last successfully published inventory is being retained safely.
DataStatus.timelineDescription: Only three time facts from the current safe projection are shown.
DataStatus.versionDescription: Breeding calculations always pin deterministic versions.
DataStatus.failureDescription: Failed parse results are never partially published; players continue to see the last complete inventory.
DataStatus.noFailureDescription: There is no stable error code and the previous snapshot is not in use.
DataStatus.fixedDescription: UUIDs can be selected and copied; source-save hashes are not exposed.

Items.title: Item inventory
Items.description: Track materials and food across every base, inspect stock trends, and see deterministic output estimates from the current shared inventory.
Items.partialTitle: Some containers could not be attributed
Items.partialDescription: Totals and production estimates include only audited containers with a confirmed base and guild owner. Unresolved stacks are intentionally excluded.
Items.inventoryDescription: Guild totals are aggregated from confirmed storage, refrigeration, feed and production-output containers.
Items.unavailable: Item inventory has not been safely resolved from a save yet.
Items.noRecipe: No supported handcraft or cooking recipe
Items.trendDescription: Hourly data is retained for 90 days and daily data for one year.
Items.noTrend: No trend samples are available for this range.
Items.capacityDescription: The estimate recursively consumes one shared virtual ledger; intermediate stock and batch output are counted exactly once.

Breeder.title: Breeding Workspace
Breeder.description: Choose a target Pal and desired passive skills. Routes are recommended from the Pals currently available to you.
Breeder.targetSettingsDescription: Choose the Pal you want to breed.
Breeder.desiredPassivesDescription: Choose up to four passive skills to inherit. Select a chosen skill to remove it.
Breeder.routePreferencesDescription: Choose whether speed, success rate or less guild borrowing matters most.
Breeder.maxFour: Choose no more than four passive skills.
Breeder.allowGuildDescription: Include Pals that guildmates have chosen to share in recommendations.
Breeder.createDescription: Calculation starts automatically. Progress and recommended routes appear on the next page.
Breeder.calculationBasisDescription: The current inventory and game data are pinned, so the result will not change when data updates.
Breeder.balancedDescription: Balances generations, available Pals, passive inheritance and borrowing.
Breeder.fastestDescription: Prioritizes fewer generations and shorter routes.
Breeder.highest_successDescription: Prioritizes concentrated passives and routes expected to be easier to complete.
Breeder.least_borrowingDescription: Prioritizes your own Pals and minimizes borrowing from guildmates.
Breeder.preferenceDisclaimer: Preferences only affect recommendation order; they never change game breeding relationships.
Breeder.searchTarget: Search by name or Paldeck number
Breeder.searchTargetPlaceholder: Enter a name or Paldeck number
Breeder.missingPassiveSources: The inventory does not contain a source for these desired passives:
Breeder.bindingDescription: An administrator must link your game character before you can create breeding jobs.
Breeder.inventoryUnavailableDescription: Wait for the next inventory sync and try again.
Breeder.gameUnavailableDescription: Breeding jobs can be created after an administrator prepares the game data.
Breeder.scoringUnavailableDescription: Ask an administrator to configure all four route preferences.
Breeder.jobNotFoundDescription: This job does not exist or this account cannot read it.
Breeder.forbiddenDescription: This account cannot perform this operation.
Breeder.requestFailedDescription: Check the current settings and try again.
Breeder.waitingNoRoute: The job did not produce a route
Breeder.pollingDescription: This page polls the real job stage without showing a fabricated percentage. Refreshing resumes the same job.
Breeder.searchLimitDescription: This result does not prove that no legal route exists. Create a new job after reducing desired passives or narrowing shared inventory.
Breeder.searchPrunedDescription: This search pruned states, so it cannot prove that no legal route exists. The pinned inputs can be recalculated by a later algorithm version.
Breeder.noLegalRouteDescription: Try fewer desired passives, more generations, or guild inventory after confirming sharing permissions.
Breeder.budgetCandidatesTitle: Best candidates within the safety budget
Breeder.budgetCandidatesDescription: The search reached its node or time budget before every route could be enumerated.
Breeder.pendingDescription: Inputs and versions are pinned while the private Worker safely claims the job.
Breeder.processingDescription: The deterministic algorithm is calculating against the pinned catalog and inventory snapshot.
Breeder.algorithm_completedDescription: Legality, scoring and route facts are complete. The result is being prepared.
Breeder.ai_enrichingDescription: Deterministic routes are ready and the final result is being saved.
Breeder.retry_pendingDescription: The Worker will resume under its lease without changing pinned inputs.
Breeder.completedDescription: Compare up to three deterministic routes and choose one whose inventory is ready.
Breeder.failedDescription: The stable error code is preserved. Check it before creating another job.
Breeder.cancelledDescription: Processing has stopped; pinned version information remains auditable.
Breeder.refreshPausedDescription: Polling reached its safety limit. Refresh the page to continue.
Breeder.stableErrorTitle: Job returned a stable error code
Breeder.saveRouteDescription: Saved routes remain available in My Plans. Saving does not advance breeding progress.
Breeder.saveMissingDescription: This route still needs inventory, but it can be saved for later.
Breeder.heuristicDisclaimer: Attempt ranges and difficulty are strategy heuristics, not verified genetic probabilities.
Breeder.savedBasisDescription: Inventory and game data used when this route was saved · {inventory} · {gameData}
Breeder.treeDefaultDescription: Initial parents → intermediate generations → final target. Connectors represent deterministic breeding relationships only.
Breeder.treeEmptyDescription: The result contains no legal breeding steps, so no fabricated nodes are shown.
Breeder.desktopTreeLabel: Desktop breeding tree; scroll horizontally within the tree
Breeder.producedByFinal: Produced by the final step of this route
